If she keeps it longer than that, then even if she expects more cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 16: asking an unrelated person for a robe
text: If a nun asks an unrelated male or female householder for a robe, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. These are the appropriate occasions: her robes are stolen or her robes are lost.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 17: accepting too many robes
text: If an unrelated male or female householder invites that nun to take many robes, she should accept at most one sarong and one upper robe. If she accepts more than that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 18: requesting a fine robe from a fund
text: If a male or female householder has set aside a robe fund for an unrelated nun, thinking, ‘With this robe fund I will buy robe-cloth and give it to nun so-and-so;’ and if that nun, without first being invited, goes to them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘Please use this robe fund to buy such-and-such robe-cloth and then give it to me,’ and she does so because she wants something fine, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 19: requesting a fine robe from a combined fund
text: If two male or female householders have set aside separate robe funds for an unrelated nun, thinking, ‘With these separate robe funds we’ll buy separate robe-cloths and give them to nun so-and-so;’ and if that nun, without first being invited, goes to them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘Please put these separate robe funds together to buy such-and-such robe-cloth and then give it to me,’ and she does so because she wants something fine, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 20: excessive prompting to get a robe
text: If a king, a king’s employee, a brahmin, or a householder sends a robe fund for a nun by messenger, saying, ‘Buy robe-cloth with this robe fund and give it to nun so-and-so,’ and the messenger goes to that nun and says, ‘Venerable, I have brought a robe fund for you. Please receive it,’ then that nun should reply, ‘We don’t receive robe funds, but we do receive allowable robe-cloth at the right time.’ If that messenger says, ‘Is there anyone who provides services for you?’ the nun, if she needs robe-cloth, should point out a monastery worker or a lay follower and say, ‘They provide services for the nuns.’ If the messenger instructs that service provider and then returns to the nun and says, ‘Venerable, I have instructed the service provider you pointed out. Please go to them at the right time and they’ll give you robe-cloth,’ then, if that nun needs robe-cloth, she should go to that service provider and prompt them and remind them two or three times, saying, ‘I need robe-cloth.’ If she then gets robe-cloth, all is well. If she does not get it, she should stand in silence for it at most six times. If she then gets robe-cloth, all is well. If she makes any further effort and then gets robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. If she does not get robe-cloth, she should go to the owners of that robe fund, or send a message, saying, ‘That nun hasn’t received any benefit from the robe fund you sent for her. Please recover what’s yours, or it might perish.’ This is the proper procedure. The second subchapter on robes is finished.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 21: becoming the owner of money
text: If a nun takes, has someone else take, or consents to gold, silver, or money being deposited for her, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 22: trading with money
text: If a nun engages in various kinds of trades involving money, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 23: bartering
text: If a nun engages in various kinds of barter, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 24: exchanging an almsbowl with fewer than five mends
text: If a nun exchanges an almsbowl with fewer than five mends for a new almsbowl, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. That nun should relinquish that almsbowl to a gathering of nuns. She should then be given the last almsbowl belonging to that gathering: ‘Nun, this bowl is yours. Keep it until it breaks.’ This is the proper procedure.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 25: storing the five tonics too long
text: After being received, the tonics allowable for sick nuns—that is, ghee, butter, oil, honey, and syrup—should be used from storage for at most seven days. If one uses them longer than that, one commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 26: taking back robe-cloth in anger
text: If a nun herself gives a robe to a nun, but then, in anger, takes it back or has it taken back, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 27: asking for thread
text: If a nun herself asks for thread, and then has weavers weave her robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 28: bribing weavers
text: If a male or female householder is having robe-cloth woven by weavers for an unrelated nun and, without first being invited, that nun goes to those weavers and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘This robe-cloth that you are weaving for me, make it long and wide; make it closely woven, well-woven, well-stretched, well-scraped, and well-combed, and perhaps I will even give you a small gift,’ then, in saying that and afterwards giving them a small gift, even a bit of almsfood, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 29: storing haste-cloth too long
text: When there are ten days left to the Kattika full moon that ends the first rainy-season residence and a haste-cloth is given to a nun, she may receive it if she regards it as urgent. She may then store it until the end of the robe season. If she stores it beyond that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

heading: Relinquishment and confession 30: diverting an offering intended for the Sangha
text: If a nun diverts to herself material support that she knows was intended for the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. The third subchapter on almsbowls is finished.

heading: Confession 1: eating garlic
text: If a nun eats garlic, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 2: removing pubic hair
text: If a nun removes hair from her private parts, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 3: masturbation
text: If a nun slaps her genitals with the palm of her hand, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 4: using a dildo
text: If a nun uses a dildo, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 5: intimate washing
text: If a nun is cleaning herself with water, she may insert two finger joints at the most. If she goes further than that, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 6: attending on a monk
text: If, when a monk is eating, a nun attends on him with drinking water or a fan, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 7: asking for raw grain
text: If a nun asks for or has someone else ask for raw grain, or she roasts it or has it roasted, or she pounds it or has it pounded, or she cooks it or has it cooked, and she then eats it, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 8: disposing of waste over a wall
text: If a nun disposes of feces or urine or trash or food scraps over a wall or over an encircling wall, or she has it disposed of in this way, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 9: disposing of waste on plants
text: If a nun disposes of feces or urine or trash or food scraps on cultivated plants, or she has it disposed of in this way, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 10: watching entertainment
text: If a nun goes to see dancing or singing or music, she commits an offense entailing confession. The first subchapter on garlic is finished.

heading: Confession 11: meeting a man in the dark
text: If, in the dark of the night without a lamp, a nun stands or talks alone with a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 12: meeting a man in a concealed place
text: If a nun stands or talks alone with a man in a concealed place, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 13: meeting a man in the open
text: If a nun stands or talks alone with a man out in the open, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 14: meeting a man on a street
text: If a nun stands or talks alone with a man on a street or in a cul-de-sac or at an intersection, or she whispers in his ear or dismisses her companion nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 15: departing without taking leave
text: If a nun visits families before the meal, sits down on a seat, and then departs without informing the owners, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 16: sitting down without permission
text: If a nun visits families after the meal, and then sits down or lies down on a seat without asking permission of the owners, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 17: putting out bedding without permission
text: If a nun visits families at the wrong time, puts out bedding without asking permission of the owners, or has it put out, and then sits down or lies down on it, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 18: complaining without reflection
text: If a nun complains about someone else because of a misunderstanding and a lack of proper reflection, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 19: cursing
text: If a nun curses herself or someone else, referring to hell or the spiritual life, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 20: crying and beating oneself
text: If a nun cries after repeatedly beating herself, she commits an offense entailing confession. The second subchapter on the dark of the night is finished.

heading: Confession 21: bathing naked
text: If a nun bathes naked, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 22: making an oversize bathing robe
text: If a nun is having a bathing robe made, it should be made the right size. This is the right size: four standard handspans long and two wide. If it exceeds that, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 23: unstitching a robe
text: If a nun, after unstitching a nun’s robe or having it unstitched, neither sews it herself nor makes any effort to have someone else sew it, and there were no obstacles, then, except if it was no more than four or five days, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 24: moving robes
text: If a nun does not move her robes for more than five days, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 25: borrowing a robe
text: If a nun wears a robe taken on loan, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 26: hindering robe-cloth for the community
text: If a nun creates an obstacle for the community to get robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 27: blocking robe-cloth distribution
text: If a nun blocks a legitimate distribution of robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 28: giving a robe to a non-monastic
text: If a nun gives a monastic robe to a householder or a male wanderer or a female wanderer, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 29: letting the robe season expire
text: If a nun lets the robe season expire because of an uncertain expectation of robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 30: blocking the ending of the robe season
text: If a nun blocks a legitimate ending of the robe season, she commits an offense entailing confession. The third subchapter on nakedness is finished.

heading: Confession 31: lying on the same bed
text: If two nuns lie down on the same bed, they commit an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 32: lying on the same sheet
text: If two nuns lie down on the same sheet and under the same cover, they commit an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 33: making a nun ill at ease
text: If a nun intentionally makes a nun ill at ease, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 34: not nursing a disciple
text: If a nun neither nurses a suffering disciple, nor makes any effort to have someone else nurse her, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 35: evicting a nun
text: If a nun gives a dwelling place to a nun, and then, in anger, throws her out or has her thrown out, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 36: socializing with a householder
text: If a nun is socializing with a householder or a householder’s offspring, the nuns should correct her like this: ‘Venerable, don’t socialize with householders or householders’ offspring. Be secluded, venerable. The Sangha praises seclusion for the sisters.’ If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop. If she then stops, all is well. If she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 37: wandering within the country
text: If a nun goes wandering without a group of travelers where it is considered risky and dangerous within her own country, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 38: wandering outside the country
text: If a nun goes wandering without a group of travelers where it is considered risky and dangerous outside her own country, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 39: wandering during the rainy season
text: If a nun goes wandering during the rainy season, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 40: not wandering after the rainy season
text: If a nun who has completed the rainy-season residence does not go wandering at least 65 to 80 kilometers, she commits an offense entailing confession. The fourth subchapter on lying down is finished.

heading: Confession 41: visiting places of pleasure
text: If a nun visits a royal house or a gallery or a park or a garden or a lotus pond, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 42: using luxurious furniture
text: If a nun uses a high or luxurious couch, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 43: spinning yarn
text: If a nun spins yarn, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 44: serving householders
text: If a nun provides services for a householder, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 45: not resolving a legal issue
text: If, when a nun is requested by a nun to resolve a legal issue, she agrees, but then neither resolves it nor makes any effort to resolve it, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 46: giving food to a non-monastic
text: If a nun personally gives fresh or cooked food to a householder or a male wanderer or a female wanderer, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 47: not relinquishing a communal robe
text: If a nun does not relinquish a communal robe, but continues to use it, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 48: not relinquishing a lodging
text: If a nun goes wandering without relinquishing her lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 49: studying worldly subjects
text: If a nun studies worldly subjects, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 50: teaching worldly subjects
text: If a nun teaches worldly subjects, she commits an offense entailing confession. The fifth subchapter on galleries is finished.

heading: Confession 51: entering a monks’ monastery
text: If a nun, knowing that there are monks in a monastery, enters it without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 52: abusing a monk
text: If a nun abuses or reviles a monk, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 53: reviling the community
text: If a furious nun reviles the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 54: eating more after refusing an offer
text: If a nun, who has been invited to a meal, refuses an offer to eat more, and then eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 55: being stingy with families
text: If a nun keeps a family to herself, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 56: spending the rainy season apart from monks
text: If a nun spends the rainy-season residence in a monastery without monks, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 57: not doing the invitation ceremony
text: If a nun who has completed the rainy-season residence does not invite correction from both Sanghas in regard to three things—what has been seen, heard, or suspected—she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 58: not going to the instruction
text: If a nun does not go to the instruction or to a formal meeting of the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 59: not seeking the instruction
text: Every half-month a nun should seek two things from the Sangha of monks: asking it about the observance day and going to it for the instruction. If she lets the half-month pass, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 60: getting medical treatment from a man
text: If a nun, alone with a man, without getting permission from the Sangha or a group, has an abscess or a wound situated on the lower part of her body ruptured by him, or split open, washed, anointed, bandaged, or unwrapped by him, she commits an offense entailing confession. The sixth subchapter on monasteries is finished.

heading: Confession 61: ordaining a pregnant woman
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a pregnant woman, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 62: ordaining a breastfeeding woman
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a woman who is breastfeeding, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 63: ordaining an untrained candidate
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 64: ordaining a trained candidate without approval
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 65: ordaining a married girl under twelve
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is less than twelve years old, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 66: ordaining an untrained married girl
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 67: ordaining a trained married girl without approval
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old and who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 68: not guiding a disciple after ordination
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a disciple, and then, for the next two years, neither guides her nor has her guided, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 69: not following a mentor
text: If a nun does not follow the mentor who gave her the full admission for two years, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 70: not sending away a new disciple
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a disciple, and then neither sends her away nor has her sent away at least 65 to 80 kilometers, she commits an offense entailing confession. The seventh subchapter on pregnant women is finished.

heading: Confession 71: ordaining an unmarried woman under twenty
text: If a nun gives the full admission to an unmarried woman who is less than twenty years old, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 72: ordaining an untrained unmarried woman
text: If a nun gives the full admission to an unmarried woman who is more than twenty years old, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 73: ordaining a trained unmarried woman without approval
text: If a nun gives the full admission to an unmarried woman who is more than twenty years old and who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 74: giving ordination while under twelve years’ seniority
text: If a nun who has less than twelve years of seniority gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 75: giving ordination without approval
text: If a nun who has twelve years of seniority gives the full admission without approval from the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 76: agreeing to stop ordaining, but then criticizing it
text: If a nun is told, ‘Venerable, you’ve given enough full admissions for now,’ and she consents, saying, ‘Fine,’ but then criticizes it afterwards, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 77: not ordaining a trainee after promising
text: If a nun tells a trainee nun, ‘If you give me a robe, venerable, I’ll give you the full admission,’ but she then neither gives her the full admission nor makes any effort to have her fully admitted, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 78: not ordaining a trainee who has followed one
text: If a nun tells a trainee nun, ‘If you follow me for two years, venerable, I’ll give you the full admission,’ but she then neither gives her the full admission nor makes any effort to have her fully admitted, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 79: ordaining one who is difficult to live with
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who is socializing with men and boys and who is temperamental and difficult to live with, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 80: ordaining without permission from family
text: If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has not been given permission by her parents or her husband, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 81: ordaining after consent expires
text: If, when a given consent has expired, a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 82: ordaining every year
text: If a nun gives full admission every year, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 83: ordaining two in the same year
text: If a nun gives the full admission to two women in the same year, she commits an offense entailing confession. The eighth subchapter on unmarried women is finished.

heading: Confession 84: using sunshades and sandals
text: If a nun who is not sick uses a sunshade and sandals, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 85: traveling in a vehicle
text: If a nun who is not sick travels in a vehicle, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 86: wearing a hip ornament
text: If a nun wears a hip ornament, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 87: wearing jewelry
text: If a nun wears jewelry, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 88: bathing in scents and colors
text: If a nun bathes with scents and colors, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 89: bathing with sesame paste
text: If a nun bathes with scented sesame paste, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 90: getting a massage from a nun
text: If a nun has a nun massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 91: getting a massage from a trainee nun
text: If a nun has a trainee nun massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 92: getting a massage from a novice nun
text: If a nun has a novice nun massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 93: getting a massage from a female householder
text: If a nun has a female householder massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 94: sitting in front without permission
text: If a nun sits down on a seat in front of a monk without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 95: asking a question without permission
text: If a nun asks a question of a monk who has not given her permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 96: not wearing a chest wrap
text: If a nun enters an inhabited area without wearing her chest wrap, she commits an offense entailing confession. The ninth subchapter on sunshades and sandals is finished.

heading: Confession 97: lying
text: If a nun lies in full awareness, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 98: abusive speech
text: If a nun speaks abusively, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 99: malicious talebearing
text: If a nun engages in malicious talebearing between nuns, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 100: instructing a householder to memorize the Teaching
text: If a nun instructs a person who is not fully ordained to memorize the Teaching, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 101: lying down with one not fully ordained
text: If a nun lies down more than two or three nights in the same sleeping place as a woman who is not fully ordained, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 102: lying down with a man
text: If a nun lies down in the same sleeping place as a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 103: teaching a man alone
text: If a nun gives a teaching of more than five or six sentences to a man, except in the presence of a woman who understands, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 104: truthfully announcing a superhuman quality
text: If a nun truthfully tells a person who is not fully ordained of a superhuman quality, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 105: announcing a nun’s grave offense
text: If a nun tells a person who is not fully ordained about a nun’s grave offense, except if the nuns have agreed, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 106: digging the earth
text: If a nun digs the earth or has it dug, she commits an offense entailing confession. The tenth subchapter on lying is finished.

heading: Confession 107: destroying plants
text: If a nun destroys a plant, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 108: speaking evasively
text: If a nun speaks evasively or harasses, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 109: complaining
text: If a nun complains or criticizes, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 110: leaving furniture outside
text: If a nun takes a bed, a bench, a mattress, or a stool belonging to the Sangha and puts it out in the open or has it put out in the open, and she then departs without putting it away, having it put away, or informing anyone, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 111: not putting away bedding
text: If a nun puts out bedding in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, or has it put out, and she then departs without putting it away, having it put away, or informing anyone, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 112: encroaching on a nun
text: If, in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, a nun arranges her sleeping place in a way that encroaches on a nun that she knows arrived there before her, with the intention that anyone who feels crowded will leave, and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 113: evicting a nun
text: If a nun, in anger, throws a nun out of a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, or has her thrown out, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 114: sitting down on an upper story
text: If a nun sits down or lies down on a bed or a bench with detachable legs on an upper story in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 115: applying excessive materials to a large dwelling
text: When a nun is building a large dwelling, then standing where there are no cultivated plants, she may apply two or three layers of roofing material, taking it as far as the doorcase and using it for fixing the door and for treating the window openings. If she applies more than that, even if she stands where there are no cultivated plants, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 116: pouring water with living beings in it
text: If a nun pours water that she knows contains living beings onto grass or clay, or has it poured, she commits an offense entailing confession. The eleventh subchapter on plants is finished.

heading: Confession 117: eating excessively at a public guesthouse
text: If a nun who is not sick eats more than one almsmeal at a public guesthouse, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 118: eating in a group
text: If a nun eats in a group, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing confession. These are the appropriate occasions: she is sick; it is the robe-giving season; it is a time of making robes; she is traveling; she is on a boat; it is a big occasion; it is a meal given by a monastic.

heading: Confession 119: accepting more than three bowlfuls
text: If a nun goes to a family and is invited to take cookies or crackers, she may accept two or three bowlfuls if she wishes. If she accepts more than that, she commits an offense entailing confession. If she accepts two or three bowlfuls, she should take it away and share it with the nuns. This is the proper procedure.

heading: Confession 120: eating at the wrong time
text: If a nun eats fresh or cooked food at the wrong time, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 121: eating stored food
text: If a nun eats fresh or cooked food that she has stored, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 122: eating ungiven food
text: If a nun eats food that has not been given, except for water and tooth cleaners, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 123: dismissing a nun during almsround
text: If a nun says to a nun, ‘Come, let’s go to the village or town for alms,’ and then, whether she has had food given to her or not, sends her away, saying, ‘Go away, I’m not comfortable talking or sitting with you, but only if I talk and sit by myself,’ and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 124: intruding on a lustful couple
text: If a nun sits down intruding on a lustful couple, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 125: sitting with a man in a concealed place
text: If a nun sits down in private on a concealed seat with a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 126: sitting alone with a man
text: If a nun sits down in private alone with a man, she commits an offense entailing confession. The twelfth subchapter on eating is finished.

heading: Confession 127: visiting families before a meal
text: If a nun who has been invited to a meal visits families beforehand or afterwards without informing an available nun, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing confession. These are the appropriate occasions: it is the robe-giving season; it is a time of making robes.

heading: Confession 128: accepting an invitation of more than four months
text: A nun who is not sick may accept an invitation to ask for requisites for four months. If she accepts one beyond that limit, except if it is a further invitation or a permanent invitation, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 129: going to see a mobilized army
text: If a nun goes to see an army, except if there is a suitable reason, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 130: staying more than three days with an army
text: If that nun has a reason for going to the army, she may stay with the army for two or three nights. If she stays longer than that, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 131: seeing an army in action
text: If a nun who is staying with an army for two or three nights goes to a battle, a troop review, a massing of the army, or a troop inspection, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 132: drinking alcohol
text: If a nun drinks this or that kind of alcoholic drink, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 133: tickling
text: If a nun tickles someone, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 134: playing in water
text: If a nun plays in water, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 135: disrespect
text: If a nun is disrespectful, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 136: scaring a nun
text: If a nun scares a nun, she commits an offense entailing confession. The thirteenth subchapter on visiting is finished.

heading: Confession 137: lighting a fire
text: If a nun who is not sick lights a fire to warm herself, or has one lit, except if there is a suitable reason, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 138: bathing too often
text: If a nun bathes at intervals of less than a half-month, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing confession. These are the appropriate occasions: it is the two-and-a-half-month period of summer and the fever season, comprising the last one-and-a-half months of summer and the first month of the rainy season; she is sick; she is working; she is traveling; there is wind and rain.

heading: Confession 139: not making stains on a new robe
text: When a nun gets a new robe, she should apply one of three kinds of stains: blue-green, mud color, or dark brown. If a nun uses a new robe without applying any of the three kinds of stains, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 140: using assigned property that has not been relinquished
text: If a nun herself assigns the ownership of a robe to a monk, a nun, a trainee nun, a novice monk, or a novice nun, and she then uses it without the other first relinquishing it, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 141: hiding a robe
text: If a nun hides a nun’s bowl, robe, sitting mat, needle case, or belt, or she has it hidden, even just for a laugh, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 142: intentionally killing a living being
text: If a nun intentionally kills a living being, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 143: using water with living beings in it
text: If a nun uses water that she knows contains living beings, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 144: reopening a settled legal issue
text: If a nun reopens a legal issue that she knows has been legitimately settled, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 145: traveling with thieves
text: If a nun knowingly travels by arrangement with a group of thieves, even just to the next inhabited area, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 146: not giving up a bad view
text: If a nun says, ‘As I understand the Buddha’s Teaching, the things he calls obstacles are unable to obstruct one who indulges in them,’ then the nuns should correct her like this: ‘No, venerable, don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for it’s not good to misrepresent the Buddha. The Buddha would never say such a thing. In many discourses the Buddha has declared the obstacles to be obstructive and how they obstruct one who indulges in them.’ If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her give up that view. If she then gives it up, all is well. If she does not, she commits an offense entailing confession. The fourteenth subchapter on fire is finished.

heading: Confession 147: living with an ejected nun
text: If a nun lives, does formal meetings, or shares a sleeping place with a nun who she knows is saying such things, who has not made amends according to the rule, and who has not given up that view, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 148: supporting a novice nun with a bad view
text: Also if a novice nun says, ‘As I understand the Buddha’s Teaching, the things he calls obstacles are unable to obstruct one who indulges in them,’ then the nuns should correct her like this: ‘No, don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for it’s not good to misrepresent the Buddha. The Buddha would never say such a thing. In many discourses the Buddha has declared the obstacles to be obstructive and how they obstruct one who indulges in them.’ If that novice nun continues as before, she should be told: ‘From today on you may not refer to the Buddha as your teacher. And, unlike other novices, you can no longer share a sleeping place with the nuns for two or three nights. Go! Away with you!’ If a nun befriends that novice nun, or she is attended on by her, lives with her, or shares a sleeping place with her, even though she knows that she has been expelled in this way, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 149: not accepting legitimate correction
text: If a nun, when legitimately corrected by the nuns, says, ‘I won’t practice this training rule until I’ve questioned a nun who is an expert on the Monastic Law,’ she commits an offense entailing confession. A nun who is training should understand, should question, should enquire. This is the proper procedure.

heading: Confession 150: disparaging the training rules
text: When the Monastic Code is being recited, if a nun says, ‘What’s the point of reciting these minor training rules, when they just lead to anxiety, oppression, and annoyance?’ then in disparaging the training rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 151: deception
text: During the half-monthly recitation of the Monastic Code, a nun might say, ‘Just now did I find out that this rule too has come down in the Monastic Code, is included in the Monastic Code, and comes up for recitation every half-month.’ If other nuns know that that nun has previously sat through at least two or three recitations of the Monastic Code, then that nun is not let off because of ignorance, and she is to be dealt with according to the rule. Further, she should be charged with deception: ‘It’s a loss for you that you don’t pay proper attention during the recitation of the Monastic Code.’ And for the act of deception, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 152: hitting in anger
text: If a nun hits a nun in anger, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 153: raising a hand in anger
text: If a nun raises a hand in anger against a nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 154: making a groundless accusation
text: If a nun groundlessly charges a nun with an offense entailing suspension, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 155: intentionally making a nun anxious
text: If a nun intentionally makes a nun anxious, thinking, ‘In this way she will be ill at ease at least for a moment,’ and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 156: eavesdropping
text: If a nun eavesdrops on nuns who are arguing and disputing, thinking, ‘I’ll hear what they say,’ and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession. The fifteenth subchapter on view is finished.

heading: Confession 157: criticizing a legitimate legal procedure
text: If a nun gives her consent to legitimate legal procedures, and then criticizes them afterwards, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 158: leaving without giving consent
text: When the Sangha is in the middle of a discussion, if a nun gets up from her seat and leaves without first giving her consent, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 159: criticizing a robe distribution
text: If a nun gives out a robe as part of a unanimous Sangha and then criticizes it afterwards, saying, ‘The nuns are diverting the Sangha’s material support according to friendship,’ she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 160: diverting gains intended for the Sangha
text: If a nun diverts to an individual material support that she knows was intended for the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 161: picking up precious things
text: If a nun picks up something precious or something regarded as precious, or she has it picked up, except within a monastery or inside a lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession. If she picks up something precious or something regarded as precious, or she has it picked up, within a monastery or inside a lodging, she should put it aside with the thought, ‘Whoever owns it will come and get it.’ This is the proper procedure.

heading: Confession 162: making an inappropriate needle case
text: If a nun has a needle case made from bone, ivory, or horn, it is to be destroyed, and she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 163: making an inappropriate bed or bench
text: If a nun is having a new bed or bench made, it is to have legs eight standard fingerbreadths long below the lowest frame. If the legs exceed that, they are to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 164: making an upholstered bed or bench
text: If a nun has a bed or a bench made upholstered with cotton down, it is to be stripped, and she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 165: making an oversize itch cloth
text: If a nun is having an itch-covering cloth made, it should be made the right size. This is the right size: four standard handspans long and two wide. If it exceeds that, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.

heading: Confession 166: making an oversize robe
text: If a nun has a robe made that is the standard robe size or larger, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession. This is the standard robe size: nine standard handspans long and six wide. The sixteenth subchapter on legitimate correction is finished.

heading: Acknowledgement 1: asking for ghee
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for ghee and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 2: asking for oil
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for oil and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 3: asking for honey
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for honey and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 4: asking for syrup
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for syrup and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 5: asking for fish
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for fish and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 6: asking for meat
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for meat and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 7: asking for milk
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for milk and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I’ve done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’

heading: Acknowledgement 8: asking for curd
text: If a nun who is not sick asks for curd and then eats it, she must acknowledge it: ‘I have done a blameworthy and unsuitable thing that is to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’
